yagmur: The bellows reek of dampness, the forge is smoking in this downpour, guard.
If rain leaks from the roof, the charcoal gets wet; if charcoal gets wet, the hearth dies.
kar: Iron quenched in the frost cracks easily; we must stoke the bellows hard.
The snow has blocked the door, but thank heavens the forge still burns; if anyone comes, we'll warm them.
ayaz: The anvil is freezing cold; whoever touches it without gloves will leave skin on the iron.
Our breath freezes in the workshop. We must throw more oak logs into the embers.
sicak: Fire rains from the heavens, and the hearth adds to it... One cannot stand by the anvil today.
Forging iron in this sweltering heat is torment; our water is nearly exhausted.
sis: The fog has trapped the smoke; you cannot see a span ahead inside the workshop.
Even the hammer blows sound muffled in the mist; it is as though the village is asleep.

yagmur: The skies have opened; if the roof leaks, the flour in the sacks will be ruined!
They say rain is a blessing, but the oven chimney smokes back and stings my eyes.
kar: Come by the hearth; in this bitter snow, a soul without warm soup will not fare well.
The snow is knee-deep; steam rises high into the sky from the fresh bread out of the oven.
ayaz: The water jar has turned to stone from the frost; my arms ache from breaking ice since dawn.
Tonight's frost is cruel; leave the oven ashes warm so the stray creatures do not freeze.
sicak: The heat made the dough rise too quickly, but the stew sours fast; we must keep it in the cool cellar.
The midday sun burns like flame; combined with the oven heat, we can scarcely breathe.
sis: They say even wolves creep into the village in this heavy fog; do not let the children outdoors.
Mist shrouds everything; I lost my bearings twice just carrying water from the fountain.

yagmur: You are soaked through... Come by the hearth, let me drape a dry shawl over your back.
The eaves are overflowing again; take care not to catch a chill keeping watch at the gate.
kar: The blizzard howls atop the ramparts... Bundle up, my guard; that wind cuts to the marrow.
The snow has silenced the village; I will keep the soup piping hot until you return from watch.
ayaz: The frost makes the floorboards creak tonight... Our firewood runs low, but the fire must not die.
Even iron freezes out there; your hands are ice, come stretch them toward the embers.
sicak: The steppe sun scorches the plains; mind the heat does not strike your head on the ramparts.
I fear the well might dry up; this relentless heat makes everyone's temper flare.
sis: The fog swallowed the gate tower whole; keep your eyes sharp on watch, my guard.
Footsteps sound deceptive in this haze; stay vigilant, your life is in our keeping.

yagmur: Rain brings abundance, yet dampness rots healing herbs; hang them under the porch at once.
The humidity stirs aches in stiff joints; I must prepare mustard poultices.
kar: When snow falls, the elders' chests begin to rattle; we must brew linden tea with honey.
By grace I gathered mountain thyme before the blizzard closed the paths; our winter cure is ready.
ayaz: Never bring frostbitten limbs directly to the fire; rub them gently with snowmelt first.
Tonight's dry freeze scorches the lungs; every hearth needs thyme steam before slumber.
sicak: This scorching heat festers wounds swiftly; we must dress them with herbal vinegar.
Sunstroke can be deadly; those working the fields must bind wet cloths about their heads.
sis: This thick mist settles heavy on the chest; those short of breath should chew mint and pine resin.
Damp ague spreads in murky weather; do not drink well water without boiling it first.

yagmur: If rain drips, the court registry is ruined; stow the parchments in leather pouches immediately.
The roof is about to leak; damp paper bleeds ink, writing today is a futile chore.
kar: The snow has surely choked the passes; the courier from Konya must be stranded at the inn.
The blizzard batters the shutter; on such winter nights, one ought to read the ancient chronicles.
ayaz: Ink has frozen solid in the inkhorn; I cannot write a letter without thawing the quill in warm ash.
Numb fingers cannot grip the reed; this biting frost slows even scholarship, guard.
sicak: The heat presses so relentlessly that sheets of parchment curl in the scribe chamber.
The mind turns sluggish under this oppressive sun; I must wait for dusk to avoid ledger mistakes.
sis: The fog turns the horizon into a deep well; where sight fails, rumors breed aplenty.
One does not survey boundaries in thick mist; the eyes easily deceive, guard.

yagmur: The brook swells in spate! If we don't open the sluices, the water will smash the millwheel.
In rain the sheep's wool drinks water, making them twice as heavy; driving them is hard toil.
kar: The snow drifts almost over the fold; the flock is penned within, but will our hay hold out?
The blizzard drives wolves toward human scent; I must unleash the hounds and keep sharp vigil.
ayaz: Tonight's frost is lethal; I wrapped the newborn lambs in felt and placed them by the hearth.
The trough at the fountain froze over; I have been breaking ice all morning to water the beasts.
sicak: The grass has withered in the sun; no graze remains, the sheep pant with tongues out in the shade.
The millrace runs shallow; the wheel barely turns at half speed, the milling will be delayed.
sis: If I lose the bell's chime in this mist, sheep will plunge off the cliff; I dare not blink.
When fog settles, the wolf's eyes glint while the shepherd is blinded; may God preserve us.

yagmur: Rain softened the earth; it is the ideal hour to dig out licorice and mandrake roots.
Dried spices spoil in damp air; I must burn resin incense in the storehouse to dry the room.
kar: Mountain snow freezes medicinal pine sap; hard to harvest, yet twice as potent in healing.
Soil under a snowy blanket carries a peculiar fragrance; in winter I brew hot spiced elixirs.
ayaz: Rose oil in the phials has congealed; the bitter chill turns soft salve into hardened wax.
When frost burns the lungs, drink boiled ginger and cinnamon; keep the inner fire burning.
sicak: The blistering heat evaporates volatile essences; I moved the musk and amber phials underground.
When parching heat strikes, scorpions and vipers creep from their crevices; watch your step.
sis: In our highlands they called this fog 'the witch's breath'; it steals both path and wits.
The haze drifted from valley to village; burning wormwood smoke clears the fogged head.

yagmur: Dampness slackened the warp threads; carpets woven in this weather will not hold even knots.
The scent of rain soaked into the fleeces; if woven before drying, the cloth will sour.
kar: When snow arrives, all folk clamor for heavy felt coats and wool socks; the shuttle never rests.
A white shroud blankets outside; sitting at the loom, I warm myself with vibrant spools of yarn.
ayaz: My fingertips throb with icy pain; there is no feeling left to spin fine silk in this chill.
The freezing cold turned the wooden loom to stone; even the shuttle slips from numb fingers.
sicak: Dry heat sets madder dye swiftly, yet makes fragile wool strands brittle.
Handling fleece in this stifling heat is torment; sweaty palms cling awkwardly to the thread.
sis: Daylight vanished into the mist; my eyes ache counting warp knots, a lantern is barely enough.
The fog coats windows like frosted pane; patterns woven in this gloom will show flaws.

yagmur: Rain washes tracks away; mud reveals quarry, yet the bowstring has slackened with moisture.
A heavy downpour deafens the woods; keep downwind or you won't stalk a single beast.
kar: Tracks in fresh snow never lie; the deer herds moved down into the valley, time to hunt.
Blizzard blinds both hunter and beast; whoever loses direction in the snow dies frozen.
ayaz: In dry frost a snapped branch cracks like gunshot; walking silently in the forest is impossible.
The horn backing of my bow has grown brittle; draw too hard in this frost and it will snap.
sicak: No wild game stirs under scorching midday sun; all quarry lies motionless in deep thickets.
In this drought game must seek water; if you intend an ambush, wait beside the spring.
sis: One does not hunt in thick mist; in mist, you are the hunted. Keep your ears tuned to the string.
Murky weather hides even bandit footprints; think twice before stepping outside the palisade.

yagmur: The heavens granted mercy, praise be; the crops drank deep, yet the plow sticks in heavy mud.
The rains overflow the gullies; unless we clear the ditch sluices, seed will rot under standing water.
kar: Snow serves as blanket to winter wheat; snow in winter means brimming granaries in harvest.
The snow exceeds knee depth; if we don't shovel the barn roof, the rafters will split under weight.
ayaz: Frost bites tender shoots to the core; we must mulch straw around the young orchard saplings.
Soil has turned to iron with the freeze; strike it with a pickaxe and sparks fly, but it won't budge.
sicak: The ground has cracked with drought; I dread the grain will wither before heads can fill.
The sun hammers like an iron mallet; no water flows in the ditch, our backs break hauling buckets.
sis: Morning fog brings blight rust to the grain; unless wind clears it by noon, ears will mildew.
You cannot see the field's edge in this mist; even the oxen lose their furrow and nudge the fence.

yagmur: Mail armor will rust in this downpour... The blade must be rubbed with sheep tallow every night.
Neither horse nor soldier gallops in mud; if foes advance in this mire, their own weight drowns them.
kar: Snow swallows sound, guard; even if enemy riders reached the rampart base, you'd barely hear hooves.
Winter raids on the steppe are ruthless; let not sentries' eyelashes freeze together, keep alert!
ayaz: The iron helm clings frozen to my brow; the bowstring is stiff, pull it rashly and it snaps.
In dry freeze the dagger hilt glazes over; keep fingers inside your gauntlets, let not blood cool.
sicak: Chainmail heats like an oven plate; standing guard under this glare is fiercer than battle.
Water in the flask has turned scalding; soldiers' tempers fray easily under such sun, beware fights.
sis: Foggy weather is outlaw weather; archers cannot sight targets, keep your blade loose in scabbard!
On watch in mist, ears must be your eyes; if twigs snap beneath the wall, cast a torch down.

yagmur: Lanes turned to mire lakes; nothing to do but stand on the threshold and wait for rain to abate.
Rain hammers upon the shingles; whoever has a dry nook in their home ought to give thanks today.
kar: If we don't shovel the rooftop snow, rafters will collapse; winter brought abundance but harsh toil.
Snow settled silently over the roofs; whoever kindles pine kindling has no yearning to wander out.
ayaz: The wind pierces to the bone; batten doors and flues so frost does not pierce the dwelling's peace.
Stones would shatter struck together in this freeze; our breath rises before us like smoke clouds.
sicak: One cannot draw breath even in shaded nooks; streets lie deserted under this oppressive glare.
The sun beats so fierce it could spark dry rocks; we pray for any whisper of cool breeze.
sis: Fog swallowed the far end of the village; you cannot see a span ahead, none know who passes.
When mist thickens, even bells and calls vanish; an eerie quiet has claimed the hamlet.
